tools.name: create_job
tools.description:
Hand off a multi-step, multi-day task that golive runs to completion, even after this session ends. Paid or irreversible steps pause for the user's approval through a link. Job types:
- launch_domain: Buy a domain, put its DNS on the configured provider, point it at your app, and confirm it resolves

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Current status of a job, what is blocking it, and what to do next.

tools.name: undo_job
tools.description: Reverses finished steps that can be undone, newest first. Purchases that can't be refunded are listed, not undone.

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: Services Gluo runs for agents (site checks, screenshots, domain availability, email setup, dependency vulnerabilities, ...), each with its exact input schema. Operations marked free can be called right away with call_api and no budget, up to a daily allowance. Anything else, or more than the allowan

tools.name: request_budget
tools.description: Request a spending budget for specific operations. Ask only for the operations and amount the task needs: the user sees the exact scope, caps and purpose, and calls outside it are refused. The approval link goes to the user, not to you.

tools.name: get_budget
tools.description: Status, spend, remaining amount and per-operation usage of a budget.

tools.name: call_api
tools.description: Make one call. Leave out budgetId to use the free tier (free operations only, daily allowance). Input must match the operation's schema exactly (extra fields are rejected). Paid calls are charged only if the answer passes Gluo's output check; repeating an identical call shortly after is free.

tools.name: close_budget
tools.description: End a budget when the task is done. Returns a signed statement of every call and charge.

tools.name: request_service
tools.description: If a task needs a service, API or action Gluo doesn't offer, describe it in a sentence or two. This is how Gluo decides what to build next. Include roughly what you'd expect it to cost if you know.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_services · Public sink: list_services.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_services · Public sink: list_services

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
